hero.filename: Votive relief to Amynos by Lysimachides (4th cent. B.C.) at the National Archaeological Museum of Athens on 22 July 2018.jpg
hero.caption:
Votive relief. Marble. Found near the Enneakrounos fountain, Athens. From the sanctuary of the hero-physician Amynos. According to the inscription above the representation the relief was dedicated by Lysimachides, son of Lysimachos, from Acharnai. The dedicator holds a model of a human leg, on which a vein stands out indicating his disease. In a recessed panel at the bottom left are represented two feet. End of the 4th century B.C. Accession number: 3526. National Archaeological Museum of Athens. Athens, Greece.
Text: Museum inscription.

images.caption: 5 worshippers (2 women, boy, 1 male youth, 1 man) approach Hygieia (head lost) standing next to a round altar with a box in her left hand, and hand of another figure is visible holding a cup (Asklepios?). H 0.32 W 0.41. Pentelic marble. Traces of blue on background, red on altar base, goddess' chiton, worshippers' shoes and hair.
